spec: tools.run_tool must never raise when the operating system refuses to start the program. Today, when subprocess.run raises OSError (for example WinError 4551, an Application Control policy blocking the executable, or a permission error), the exception escapes and `python harness/run.py check` crashes with a traceback. Required: run_tool catches OSError from subprocess.run and returns a Result with exit_code -3, empty stdout, stderr '<name>: could not start (<the OSError text>)', and the resolved executable path. The lint check already turns a negative exit code into COULD NOT RUN, so with this change a blocked lint tool is reported, not a crash. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng01_tool_oserror.py, unittest, start with the line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): patch tools.subprocess.run to raise OSError('blocked by policy') and patch tools.resolve to return a fake path; assert run_tool returns exit_code -3, that 'could not start' and 'blocked by policy' are in stderr, and that it does not raise. Import the package as `from engine import tools` (tests run from the harness directory).

When `gate prepare` finds the quality gate failed it prints 'gate: quality gate FAILED; the security gate does not run on code whose tests do not pass (REQ-6.1.4)' even when the test suite passed and the failure was something else (a negative-test gap, missing coverage report). Required: the message names the failing quality checks by their outcome names, e.g. 'gate: quality gate FAILED (negative-tests, coverage-range); the security gate does not run until the quality gate passes (REQ-6.1.4)'. The words 'tests do not pass' must not appear unless the failing outcome is test-suite. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng03_quality_gate_message.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): patch engine.gate.prepare to return ([an Outcome named negative-tests that failed, an Outcome named test-suite that is clean], [], {...}) and engine.config.load, call engine.__main__.cmd_gate with ['prepare','unit=U1','run=1','base=HEAD','head=HEAD'] while patching engine.gitutil.rev to return a fake sha, capture stdout, and assert 'negative-tests' is in the FAILED line and 'tests do not pass' is not. Build Outcomes with engine.outcome.Outcome.found(name, summary, findings, blocking=True) and Outcome.clean(name, summary).

`review unit=U run=N` launches the reviewer on .engine/work/handoff-U-N.md without checking it against the prepared gate run (.engine/work/gate-U-N.json, written by `gate prepare`, which holds 'base' and 'head'). A handoff generated for a different range wastes a long model run whose verdict `gate submit` then refuses. Required: before launching, cmd_review reads the prepared state; if it is missing, refuse with 'review: COULD NOT RUN — no prepared gate run U#N; run `gate prepare` first' and exit 2; if the handoff's 'range: <base>..<head>' line does not match the prepared base and head (compare full or 12-character prefixes), refuse with a message containing 'handoff range' and 'prepared' and exit 2. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng05_review_stale_handoff.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): in a temporary directory write .engine/work/handoff-U1-1.md containing a line 'range: aaaa..bbbb' and .engine/work/gate-U1-1.json with base 'aaaa' and head 'cccc'; set ENGINE_REVIEWER_CMD to something harmless; call engine.__main__.cmd_review(root, ['unit=U1','run=1']); assert it returns 2, that stdout mentions the mismatch, and that subprocess.run was never called (patch engine.__main__.subprocess or the subprocess module used inside cmd_review). Also assert a missing gate json returns 2.

The engine's own security-gate definition cites OWASP MASVS (a mobile standard). On a project whose track is 'web' every MASVS citation is reported as a finding ('platform not in the index'), so every fresh web project starts with a non-blocking finding it can do nothing about except a hand-written acceptance. Required: when the project's track is not 'android', MASVS citations are counted as not applicable to the track (like the accepted-unindexed ones) and not reported as findings; the outcome's summary says how many were set aside as 'not applicable to track web'. Android projects keep today's behaviour. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng07_citations_track.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): call engine.checks.citations.verify_text (or the smallest function that decides per citation) with a text citing 'OWASP MASVS-STORAGE' once with track 'web' and once with track 'android', and assert the web call reports no finding for it while the android call does. If verify_text has no track parameter, add a keyword parameter track=None and pass cfg.track from run().

license-policy reports 'no third-party components yet' for a project whose page loads a library from a CDN, because it only reads dependency manifests and lockfiles. Required: the check also scans tracked .html/.htm files for <script src=...> and <link ... href=...> whose URL starts with http:// or https:// (a remote origin). Each one is a third-party component: a remote reference without an integrity= attribute is a blocking finding '<file>: <url> is loaded from a remote origin without Subresource Integrity'; one with integrity is a non-blocking finding '<file>: <url> is third-party code from a remote origin (pinned by integrity); a disconnected deployment cannot load it — vendor it'. Files under a directory named vendor are reported in the summary as vendored third-party files counted by number. When nothing remote and no manifest exist the outcome stays nothing-to-check-yet as today. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng12_html_third_party.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): unit-test a helper engine.checks.license_policy.remote_references(html_text) returning a list of (url, has_integrity) pairs: a script with integrity, a stylesheet link without, a relative /vendor/x.js (not remote), and an inline script with no src; assert exactly the two remote ones with the right flags.

The very first commit of a freshly placed project is refused by the governance pre-commit rule, because placing the harness stages the governed files (.engine/rules/*) and no changelog row exists yet. Files exactly as the engine placed them are not a human governance change. Required: in staged_problems, a staged governed file whose current content hash (sha256 of the bytes with CRLF converted to LF) equals the hash recorded for it in .engine/harness/placed.json under 'files' is not counted as a governance change. Edited files are still counted. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng13_governance_placement.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): unit-test a helper engine.governance.unchanged_since_placement(root, rel_path) -> bool: write placed.json with the sha256 of a file's LF content and assert True; edit the file and assert False; a file absent from placed.json is False. Compute the hash the same way distribute.py records it (read it to see).

The placed project pre-commit hook (.engine/harness/hooks/pre-commit.py, shipped from harness/engine/dist/hooks/pre-commit.py) computes ROOT as three parents up from its own file, which since the four-folder move is the .engine directory, not the project; it then cannot import the engine ('No module named engine') and every commit fails. Required: ROOT is the project root: four levels up from the file (.engine/harness/hooks/pre-commit.py -> project), matching guard.py's HERE.parent.parent.parent from the hooks directory. Tests (new file harness/selftest/test_eng14_pre_commit_root.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.'): read the source text of harness/engine/dist/hooks/pre-commit.py (locate it relative to the engine package: pathlib.Path(engine.__file__).parent / 'dist' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit.py'), find the ROOT assignment, evaluate the same expression for a fake path '/p/.engine/harness/hooks/pre-commit.py' by substituting that path for __file__ (for example with a small regex extracting the parent chain or the parents[...] index), and assert it yields '/p'. Keep the test independent of git.

The reviewer driver writes a verdict JSON whose 'summary' field embeds the model's own free-text verdict block, and models invent facts in it ('model: gpt-4o', 'harness_version: 1.0', 'tier: standard') that contradict the record. Required: the driver never stores the model-written verdict block; it builds the summary block itself from the run's recorded facts (verdict, tier, run, range, control_shaped, manifest_result, completeness_blocks, platform_surface, scan_verdict, open_findings, blocking_findings, tickets_opened, reviewer_class, model, attested_by placeholder, checklist_version, harness_version) in the same '<!-- engine:block verdict-block -->' fenced format, through one function render_summary(v) where v is the verdict dict. Tests (append a new test class to harness/selftest/test_reviewers.py is NOT allowed; create harness/selftest/test_eng15_verdict_identity.py, first line '# © 2026 Casey Houle. All rights reserved.', loading the driver the way test_reviewers.py does with importlib from the reviewers directory beside the package): call render_summary with a dict whose model is 'gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M (gemma4; 31.3B)' and harness_version '0.1.0-dev+abc' and assert both appear verbatim, the block markers are present, and 'gpt-4o' does not.
